detail: supported
- **Performance:** The method avoids unnecessary loading of occluded blocks by ensuring that visibility tests are performed in occlusion order [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method avoids unnecessary loading of occluded blocks by ensuring visibility tests are performed in occlusion order. Source [S1] explicitly states in section 3.6.2 that the goal is to provide a list of bricks ordered from closest to furthest to 'avoid as much as possible performing tests on blocks located behind other blocks... which could indeed lead to the unnecessary loading of an occluded block.' It further explains that the N3-tree structure allows for an 'easy traversal of its nodes in occlusion order' (ordre d'occultation), ensuring that any node already reached cannot be occluded by a node reached later. This directly supports the claim.
supported
The N3-tree structure facilitates this by allowing easy traversal in occlusion order [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the N3-tree structure facilitates easy traversal in occlusion order. The provided text explicitly confirms this in the section 'Parcours ordonné de la structure', stating: 'La structure de N3 -tree que nous avons utilisé a l'avantage de permettre un parcours aisé de ses noeuds dans l'ordre d'occultation' (The N3-tree structure we used has the advantage of allowing an easy traversal of its nodes in occlusion order). The notes also summarize this fact.
supported
It was developed to optimize visibility detection by providing a list of bricks ordered from closest to furthest, thereby minimizing the loading of occluded blocks [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method was developed to optimize visibility detection by providing a list of bricks ordered from closest to furthest to minimize the loading of occluded blocks. Source [S1] explicitly states in section 3.6.2 that to avoid unnecessary loading of occluded blocks, it is preferable to provide the visibility detection step with a list of bricks ordered from closest to furthest. It further explains that while the tree traversal provides an occlusion order, a strict distance sort is applied to prioritize loading nearest bricks, which improves efficiency and reduces the risk of testing occluded blocks.
supported
This method generates a list of spatial bricks ordered from closest to furthest relative to the viewpoint to avoid testing blocks behind untested unloaded blocks [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method generates a list of spatial bricks ordered from closest to furthest to avoid testing blocks behind untested unloaded blocks. Source [S1] explicitly states in section 3.6.2 that the goal is to provide a list of bricks ordered from closest to furthest to avoid testing blocks located behind other untested/unloaded blocks. It further details the process: performing a depth-first traversal of the N3-tree, imposing an order based on the viewpoint direction (axes chosen based on view vector components), and applying a sorting step to create a list strictly ordered by distance. All specific details mentioned in the claim (ordered list, closest to furthest, avoiding testing behind untested blocks, N3-tree, depth-first, axis selection based on view vector) are present in the evidence.
supported

It states: '$V_{xyz}$ le vecteur direction du point de vue' (interpreted as the component of the viewpoint direction vector, consistent with the subscript xyz and the context of axis-based traversal) and '$N$ le nombre de subdivision des noeuds' (N is the number of subdivisions of the nodes). Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

It solves the problem of unnecessary data loading by ensuring that visibility tests are performed in an order where any previously reached node cannot be occluded by a subsequently reached node [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method solves the problem of unnecessary data loading by ensuring visibility tests are performed in an order where any previously reached node cannot be occluded by a subsequently reached node. Source [S1] explicitly states in the section 'Parcours ordonné de la structure': 'La structure de N3-tree... permet un parcours aisé de ses noeuds dans l'ordre d'occultation, c'est à dire en imposant que tout noeuds déjà atteint ne pourra être occulté par un noeud atteint dans la suite du parcours.' It also mentions in section 3.6.2 that this ordering is done 'Pour éviter au maximum d'effectuer des tests sur des blocs situés derrière d'autres blocs... (ceci pourrait en effet entraîner le chargement inutile d'un bloc occulté)'. Thus, the evidence fully supports the claim.
supported
- **N3-tree:** A hierarchical structure where each node represents a grid of children with $N$ subdivisions along each axis [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the N3-tree is a hierarchical structure where each node represents a grid of children with N subdivisions along each axis. The evidence explicitly mentions 'La structure de N3-tree', describes it as a hierarchy ('structure hiérarchique'), and defines 'N' as 'le nombre de subdivision des noeuds' (the number of subdivisions of the nodes). It further details the traversal of 'sous noeuds (parcours de la grille représentant le noeud)' (child nodes (traversal of the grid representing the node)) based on axes (x, y, z). Thus, the evidence supports the definition provided in the claim.
supported

It sets itself apart from sibling methods by integrating view-dependent axis prioritization directly into a depth-first traversal of the N3-tree structure, followed by a lightweight distance sort [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method integrates view-dependent axis prioritization into a depth-first traversal of the N3-tree, followed by a lightweight distance sort. The evidence confirms: 1) It performs a depth-first traversal ('traversée de l'arbre en profondeur d'abord'). 2) It uses view-dependent axis prioritization ('imposant à chaque niveau un ordre de parcours... selon les axes... choisit en fonction de la direction du point de vue'). 3) It follows this with a sort to order by distance ('La liste de briques obtenue... est donc retriée... Un tel ordre serait pourtant utile afin de charger en priorité les briques les plus proches'). 4) The evidence notes that sorting a list already ordered by a close criterion allows rapid convergence, implying it is lightweight/efficient ('convergence rapide... sans aucun surcoût'). All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported
